did: You asked what the My data rows with no Play button were. They were recordings this phone had let go once home kept them, and the clock time on each read like a length. Now each row starts with the first words home heard in it, then when it was recorded and how long it is, then where it is and its size. It plays from this phone, or from home when the phone let its copy go. If a Play doesn't get its audio, a notice says so over the list. The server change that sends the length and words went in first. Two of the other tasks had already landed or been retired, and I wrote up how to archive old Korean word sets for a fresh session to build.

calls.title: How a recording's row reads in My data
options: words first, then when and how long, then where and size
keep one line and add the length as m:ss
calls.why: You read 13:37 as a length, so m:ss would repeat the confusion, and the words are what tell one recording from another.
calls.undo: Reorder the row's lines and change itemLine and lengthOf in My data's words.

calls.title: Which rows offer Play from home
options: only where home says it gives the audio back
every row, saying a refusal after the tap
only what is on this phone
calls.why: Home owns which recordings it plays back, so the phone shows Play exactly where it will work.
calls.undo: Drop playsBack from home's kept list and offer Play only where the audio is on this phone.

calls.title: Who archives an old Korean word set
options: you, from My data, with a hint on sets not opened in a while
automatically after a set goes unused
calls.why: The phone records only when a set was first opened, not when it was last used, so a rule could pull lines you still drill out of Read aloud.
calls.undo: Add a rule that archives a set, and drop the Archive control.
